summary: Redwood AE+SE ran a hosted API demo focused on embeddings and reranking for ZenithSearch's relevance use case. Discussed integration paths (hosted API vs Dedicated), security/compliance needs (SOC2, SSO, KMS), performance expectations, and next steps to run a short pilot and benchmark using customer query logs.
meeting_header: Date: 2027-10-18 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Lena Park; Diego Morales; Amir Patel; Sofia Ruiz; Greg Holt; Maya Li
transcript:
00:00 Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. Diego will do the technical walkthrough.
00:08 Amir Patel: Hey thanks, excited. we have about 45 minutes, we wanted to see embeddings + rerank flow for improving our site search relevance.
00:15 Diego Morales: Great, i'll share my screen, demo deck and a quick live call to the hosted API. note: i'm using a dev key with limited qps.
00:29 Sofia Ruiz: quick context, we run a hybrid infra, currently Algolia for fast results and an internal reranker for final score. main pain is precision on long tail queries and cost at scale.
00:42 Diego Morales: understood, we'll show two flows: 1) embed + vector store for retrieval and 2) a rerank endpoint that takes candidate set and scores them with contextual embeddings.
00:56 Lena Park: high level: hosted API is fastest to integrate, Dedicated gives predictable throughput if you need it, and Private is for VPC/on-prem requirements.
01:10 Greg Holt: on the security side, we need SOC2 attestations, SSO support (SAML), and a KMS/HSM option for keys. also data residency in EU for some customers.
01:22 Diego Morales: we support SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, and key management integrations. for hosted we offer customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. those details are in the security pack i'll share. (link: https://redwood.example/security-pack.pdf)
01:40 Maya Li: Great. for the reranker, what's the typical latency? we need sub 200ms for the last-mile ranking.
01:47 Diego Morales: typical rerank latency depends on model size and batch size. for small encoder-only models you can see 50-120ms p99 in hosted, bigger cross-encoders push higher. we have options to quantize and pick smaller reranker models to hit 200ms SLO. there's a tradeoff cost vs latency.
02:06 Amir Patel: how does the rerank endpoint integrate with our current stack? we call an API with candidate doc ids and content?
02:13 Diego Morales: yes, the pattern: retrieve candidate docs from your index, then call Redwood rerank endpoint with the query + candidate payload (we support id+metadata or raw text). response returns scores and we pick top-K. we also show an embeddings vector-only flow where retrieval is via similarity.
02:32 Sofia Ruiz: any rate limits? our peak queries are ~800 qps during events, average 200 qps.
02:39 Lena Park: for hosted, rate limits can be increased with committed usage; if you need guaranteed throughput we recommend Dedicated with reserved GPU pools. Diego: maybe mention autoscaling/throughput details.
02:50 Diego Morales: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and autoscaling rules; you can configure burst capacity. also smart routing can fall back to a cheaper model if capacity is constrained, which helps availability.
03:09 Amir Patel: about relevance testing  we have click logs and labeled qrels. can we run end-to-end evals?
03:16 Diego Morales: yes, Redwood Optimize includes eval harnesses to run rerank experiments, run A/B tests and track metrics. we can ingest your qrels and run NDCG/MRR checks; plus regression alerts if new model variants drop quality.
03:30 Lena Park: i'll note that Optimize is an add-on but it's useful for your pre/post rollout checks.
03:36 Sofia Ruiz: what's the onboarding for the pilot? we want a 2-week pilot hitting production-like traffic.
03:42 Lena Park: typical pilot: share sample logs (Sofia), we run bench on hosted with your queries, provide latency/cost estimates; if you need sustained throughput we propose a short Dedicated eval.
03:52 Diego Morales: for benchmarking i'll run a script against a subset of your logs. i'll produce a spreadsheet with per-query latency, tokens, and cost estimates. i'll share the runbook link and sample data upload location. (link: https://redwood.example/benchmarks/runbook)
04:10 Greg Holt: regarding network, for hosted we need to know egress IPs and firewall rules; for Private/Dedicated we will need VPC peering or private link.
04:19 Diego Morales: yes, we'll send the VPC peering doc. for hosted we also have IP allowlist and can support private egress through customer-controlled NAT in some regions.
04:33 Amir Patel: any hard blockers: data retention? we need logs not retained beyond 30 days and ability to opt-out of data usage for model training.
04:41 Lena Park: we have data retention settings, and enterprise contracts include options to opt out of training data usage and set retention windows. we'll include that in the contract.
04:51 Maya Li: can you demo the rerank call quickly?
05:00 Diego Morales: sure. switching to Postman view, payload looks like: {query: "how to reset password", candidates: [{id: "doc1", text: "..."}, ...]} and response gives scores. note: transcript may be a bit off  i'm paraphrasing the JSON.
05:18 Diego Morales: (typing) sending call... response in ~85ms for this small cross-encoder on hosted dev cluster. here's sample response: ["doc3: 0.95","doc1:0.72","doc7:0.64"].
05:33 Sofia Ruiz: that's promising, though we'd want to try it on longer docs and multi-lingual content.
05:40 Diego Morales: we support multi-lingual models and also embedding-based reranks; sometimes combo retrieval+rerank is best.
05:48 Lena Park: note about cost: rerank cross-encoders are more expensive per request than embedding/dot-product scoring. Optimize can suggest model/quantization to reduce cost.
05:59 Amir Patel: any customers running this at our scale?
06:03 Lena Park: yes, we have several search-first customers; i'll share anonymized references and a case study. (link: https://redwood.example/case-studies/search)
06:15 Greg Holt: legal/procurement question  we need standard MSAs and also DPAs for EU. can you send those?
06:22 Lena Park: yes, legal will share MSA and DPA templates; i'll attach to the follow-up.
06:29 Diego Morales: quick note on observability: Console shows token-level cost, per-route latency, traces and ability to roll back model variants. you can also set canary rollout policies.
06:42 Sofia Ruiz: sounds good. if we do the pilot, we want a gating criteria: no worse than current NDCG-100 drop and p99 latency < 200ms.
06:52 Lena Park: perfect, we'll include those as pilot success metrics.
07:00 Amir Patel: ok recap?
07:03 Lena Park: recap: 1) Lena to send pricing + pilot contract 2) Diego to share benchmark runbook and run initial bench on provided logs 3) Customer provides sample logs and confirms network requirements 4) schedule pilot kickoff week of 2027-10-25.
07:20 Maya Li: thanks everyone.
07:22 Diego Morales: thanks, i'll drop links in chat.
07:26 (meeting ends)
